name: SikaShield P24 PE Argo 3 mm
paste:
SIKASHIELD® P24 PE ARGO 3 MM: SPECIFICATION CLAUSE SET

Source: SikaShield® P24 PE Argo 3 mm, April 2023, Version 01.02 (https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/l/sikashield-p24-peargo3mm.pdf)
Draft for specifier review. Wording, values and standards are quoted from that data sheet; where it is silent the clause says 'Refer to manufacturer.' Confirm the current edition before issue.

1 SCOPE
1.1 Work included. Provide SikaShield® P24 PE Argo 3 mm where documented, installed or applied in accordance with this clause and the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (April 2023, Version 01.02).
1.2 Product description. SikaShield® P24 PE Argo 3 mm is an APP modified bituminous waterproofing membrane with a thickness of 3 mm. It is reinforced with a non-woven polyester fabric dimensionally stabilised with glass fibre and is flexible at 0 °C. The top surface is coated with sand, which ensures the bond of the overlying layer and fast welding of the joints. The underside of the product has a burn-off film for easy torch-application.
1.3 Intended uses stated by the manufacturer. The Product is used as a waterproofing membrane for:
    - Balconies
    - Terraces
    - Flat roofs under protective layers or ballast
    - Sloped roofs
    - Wet areas
    - Basements and other below ground structures
    - Horizontal reinforced concrete slabs, decks and podiums
    - Vertical reinforced concrete walls
1.4 Intended uses stated by the manufacturer - The Product is used as a.
    - Base sheet in multi-layer systems
1.5 Intended uses stated by the manufacturer - Please note.
    - The Product is not suitable for roofs permanently exposed to UV radiation.

2 MATERIALS
2.1 Product. SikaShield® P24 PE Argo 3 mm
    - Product type as printed on the data sheet: Plastomeric bituminous membrane surfaced with sand and flexible at 0 °C ( Formerly Index Argo 3mm )
    - Supplier as printed on the data sheet: Sika Australia Pty Limited, ABN 12 001 342 329, aus.sika.com, Tel: 1300 22 33 48
2.2 Approvals / certificates.
    - CE marking and declaration of performance based on EN 13707:2004+A2:2009 Flexible sheets for waterproofing — Reinforced bitumen sheets for roof waterproofing
    - CE marking and declaration of performance based on EN 13969:2004/A1:2006 Flexible sheets for waterproofing — Bitumen damp proof sheets including bitumen basement tanking sheets
2.3 Standards and test methods cited in the data sheet. Cited as written in the data sheet. A citation is not a statement that the product complies with it; conformity is stated only where the data sheet says so (see the approvals clause and the statements quoted in the other clauses).
    - EN 13707:2004+A2: listed under approvals, certificates or standards. Where: Approvals / Certificates (p.1).
    - EN 13969:2004: listed under approvals, certificates or standards. Where: Approvals / Certificates (p.1).
    - EN 1848-1: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Product Information > Packaging (p.1).
    - EN 1849-2: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Product Information > Effective thickness (p.2).
    - EN 12311-1: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Elongation at maximum tensile force (p.2); Technical Information > Maximum tensile force (p.2).
    - EN 12310-1: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Resistance to tear (p.2).
    - EN 12317-1: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Joint shear resistance (p.2).
    - EN 1109: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Flexibility at low temperature (p.2).
    - EN 1928: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Watertightness (p.2).
2.4 Characteristics stated by the manufacturer.
    - Fully bonded system ensures reliable waterproofing
    - Easy to install by torching method
    - Fully bonded
    - Good durability
    - Good mechanical properties (tensile, tear, shear)
2.5 Composition.
    | Composition | APP modified bitumen |
    | Reinforcing material | non-woven polyester fabric dimen- |
    | sionally stabilised with glass fibre |
    (Table as printed; a cell that wraps appears over several rows.)
2.6 Appearance and colour.
    | Top surface | Sand |
    | Bottom Surface | Polyethylene foil |
2.7 Properties stated by the manufacturer.
    - Flexibility at low temperature: ≤ 0 °C (EN 1109)
2.8 Maximum tensile force.
    | Longitudinal (MD) | 400 N/50 mm ± 80 N/50 mm |
    | Transversal (CMD) | 300 N/50 mm ± 60 N/50 mm |
    Test method printed: (EN 12311-1)
2.9 Elongation at maximum tensile force.
    | Longitudinal (MD) | 35 % ± 15 % |
    | Transversal (CMD) | 40 % ± 15 % |
    Test method printed: (EN 12311-1)
2.10 Resistance to tear.
    | Longitudinal (MD) | 140 N ± 42 N |
    | Transversal (CMD) | 140 N ± 42 N |
    Test method printed: (EN 12310-1)
2.11 Joint shear resistance.
    | Longitudinal (MD) | 350 N/50 mm ± 70 N/50 mm |
    | Transversal (CMD) | 250 N/50 mm ± 50 N/50 mm |
    Test method printed: (EN 12317-1)
2.12 Watertightness.
    | Method B, 24 hours at 60 kPa | Pass |
    Test method printed: (EN 1928)
2.13 Packaging, shelf life and storage.
    - Shelf life: 12 months from date of production
2.14 Packaging.
    | Roll width | 1.0 m |
    | Roll length | 10.0 m |
    | Refer to the current price list for available packaging variations. |
    (Table as printed; a cell that wraps appears over several rows.)
    Test method printed: (EN 1848-1)
2.15 Storage conditions. The Product must be stored in original unopened and undamaged packaging in dry conditions and temperatures between +5 °C and +35 °C. Protect the Product from direct weather exposure and sunlight. Store in a vertical position. Pallets may be stacked on top of the rolls if all following conditions are met:
    - The rolls have a wooden board on top, separating them from the pallet above.
    - The weight of the pallet above is equal to or less than the weight of the rolls.
    Always refer to packaging.

3 SUBSTRATE PREPARATION
3.1 General. Prepare substrates in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (April 2023, Version 01.02) and the requirements below. Inspect the substrate against these requirements before application.
3.2 Substrate condition. The substrate surface must be uniform, firm, smooth and free of any sharp protrusion or burrs, clean, dry, free of grease, laitance, oil, dust and loosely adhering particles.
3.3 Priming.
    - Apply Sika® Igolflex P10+ primer at a rate of 6-8m2 per litre.
    - Note: Consumption rates will vary depending on substrate type and porosity.

4 APPLICATION
4.1 General. Apply in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (April 2023, Version 01.02) and the requirements below.
4.2 Effective thickness.
    | Effective thickness | 3.0 mm ± 0.2 mm |
    Test method printed: (EN 1849-2)
4.3 System design. Consider the following when designing the system:
    - The supporting structure must be of sufficient structural strength to support all new and existing layers of the system build-up.
    - If used as a roof system, the complete system must be designed to withstand and be secured against wind uplift loadings.
4.4 Important.
    - Unrolling at low temperatures
    - At low temperatures, the membrane becomes less flexible. 1. Be careful when unrolling to avoid damaging the membrane.
4.5 Important.
    - Damage through footwear
    - Footwear with spikes or sharp protrusions may puncture the membrane. 1. Use footwear with a flat profile when walking over the membrane.
4.6 Important.
    - Damage through overheating
    - The polyester melts at +260 °C. If it is damaged through overheating, the membrane becomes unusable. 1. Keep moving the flame while torching to avoid overheating the membrane.
4.7 Important.
    - Reduced adhesion through insufficient heating
    - Make sure to heat the membrane sufficiently. If it is not sufficiently heated, the adhesion to the substrate, between layers or on the overlaps will be reduced. 1. If the membrane does not adhere to other elements, lift and retorch the unbonded areas.
4.8 Important.
    - Application at less than +5 °C
    - When applying the membranes at temperatures lower than +5 °C, use heating equipment to ensure that the substrate temperature is within the given temperature range.
4.9 Important.
    - Application on sloped surfaces
    - For slopes with an inclination greater than 15 %, multi-layered roofs must be carefully designed and, if necessary, integrated with mechanical fastenings.
    - Seasonal symbol
    - Note: If a seasonal symbol is printed on the roll’s label, it is advisable to use the membrane during the indicated season.
    - Tackiness at high temperatures
    - Note: When laying the membrane at high temperatures, the integral adhesive will become 'tacky' and may restrict laying operations.
4.10 Important.
    - Avoid coinciding joints
    - To avoid coinciding joints, lay the membranes parallel to one another. When applying on another bituminous membrane, make sure to straddle the overlaps of the previous layer. 1. Unroll the membrane. 2. Align the membrane. 3. Re-roll the membrane before application.
4.11 Membrane overlaps. 1. Overlap the membranes by a minimum of 100 mm on the sides and 150 mm on each end or as specified by the supplier. 2. At the end overlap, cut off a corner measuring 100 mm per side at an angle of 45°.
4.12 Torching. 1. Heat the substrate and the backing film on the underside of the membrane with a gas burner.
    - When the backing film starts to melt, the membrane is ready to stick. 2. Roll the heated membrane forward and press it firmly against the substrate to bond it. 3. Make sure a bead of melted bitumen is visible along the full length of the overlap sides and ends when laying.
4.13 Torching - Suitable substrates for torching.
    - Concrete
    - Perlite screed
    - Bituminous membranes with a smooth surface
    - Coatings (check the compatibility)
    - Brick masonry
    - Cementitious screeds
4.14 Detailing.
    - 1. Use a sharp knife to cut in all details such as internal and external corners, upstands, vent pipes, drains, support metalwork etc.
    - Refer to the relevant method statement for further information on detailing.
4.15 Further information. Application of torch-applied membranes; Note: Always make reference to local regulations, standards, guidelines and established practice when using torch-applied membranes.
    - Method Statement - Roofing build-up with bituminous membranes
    - Method Statement — Bituminous membranes for below ground

5 QUALITY CONTROL AND TESTING
5.1 Hold point. Before each application, measure and record the conditions in clause 5.2 and compare them with the manufacturer's limits. HOLD POINT: do not proceed until the Superintendent has released the hold point.
5.2 Ambient air temperature.
    | Maximum | +40 °C |
    | Minimum | +5 °C |
5.3 Relative air humidity.
    | Maximum | 80 % |
5.4 Substrate temperature.
    | Maximum | +40 °C |
    | Minimum | +5 °C |
5.5 Test methods printed beside stated values. Each value is as printed in the data sheet with its test method.
    - Packaging: Roll width | 1.0 m; Roll length | 10.0 m; Refer to the current price list for available packaging variations. (EN 1848-1)
    - Effective thickness: Effective thickness | 3.0 mm ± 0.2 mm (EN 1849-2)
    - Maximum tensile force: Longitudinal (MD) | 400 N/50 mm ± 80 N/50 mm; Transversal (CMD) | 300 N/50 mm ± 60 N/50 mm (EN 12311-1)
    - Elongation at maximum tensile force: Longitudinal (MD) | 35 % ± 15 %; Transversal (CMD) | 40 % ± 15 % (EN 12311-1)
    - Resistance to tear: Longitudinal (MD) | 140 N ± 42 N; Transversal (CMD) | 140 N ± 42 N (EN 12310-1)
    - Joint shear resistance: Longitudinal (MD) | 350 N/50 mm ± 70 N/50 mm; Transversal (CMD) | 250 N/50 mm ± 50 N/50 mm (EN 12317-1)
    - Flexibility at low temperature: ≤ 0 °C (EN 1109)
    - Watertightness: Method B, 24 hours at 60 kPa | Pass (EN 1928)
5.6 Basis of the stated values. All technical data stated in this Product Data Sheet are based on laboratory tests. Actual measured data may vary due to circumstances beyond our control.
5.7 Other tests. For any test method, sampling frequency or acceptance criterion not stated in this clause: refer to manufacturer and the project specification.

6 WARRANTY AND DOCUMENTATION
6.1 Documents to be obtained and submitted. Obtain the current issue of each document before ordering and submit it with the product submission. Documents are listed as published on the manufacturer's website.
    - Product Data Sheet: SikaShield® P24 PE Argo 3 mm, April 2023, Version 01.02, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/l/sikashield-p24-peargo3mm.pdf
6.2 Ecology, health and safety. This product is an article as defined in article 3 of regulation (EC) No 1907/2006 (REACH). It contains no substances which are intended to be released from the article under normal or reasonably foreseeable conditions of use. A safety data sheet following article 31 of the same regulation is not needed to bring the product to the market, to transport or to use it. For safe use follow the instructions given in the product data sheet. Based on our current knowledge, this product does not contain SVHC (substances of very high concern) as listed in Annex XIV of the REACH regulation or on the candidate list published by the European Chemicals Agency in concentrations above 0,1 % (w/w).
6.3 Maintenance.
    - Check the functionality of the auxiliary works, flashings, drainage outlets, overflow pipes etc.
    - Remove any leaves, moss and other vegetation, which could cause ponding on the roof and overload the drainage system.
    - To maintain the function of the roof waterproofing membrane during its lifespan, it is advisable to arrange periodically for inspection of the membrane and detailing.
6.4 Warranty. Obtain any product or installation warranty in writing from the manufacturer or its authorised applicator and file it with the project records. Warranty terms: refer to manufacturer.
    - Legal notes: In practice, the differences in materials, substrates and actual site conditions are such that no warranty in respect of merchantability or of fitness for a particular purpose, nor any liability arising out of any legal relationship whatsoever, can be inferred either from this information, or from any written recommendations, or from any other advice offered.
6.5 Local restrictions. Please note that as a result of specific local regulations the declared data for this product may vary from country to country. Please consult the local Product Data Sheet for the exact product data.
6.6 Application records. Record the product name, batch numbers, dates, areas treated and the conditions measured under clause 5.2, and include the records in the project documentation.
